name: 15f dpo one pair
title: DPO raises the winner and lowers the loser relative to the reference
subtitle: One preference pair; log probabilities of whole responses; β = 0.1; no reward model and no sampling

steps.caption: Before training the policy equals the reference, so both log ratios are 0, the margin is 0, the sigmoid is 0.5 and the loss is ln 2 = 0.693 for every pair.
Training raises the winner's log probability above the reference and pushes the loser's below it. The loss reads only the gap between the two log ratios.
Final state: winner log ratio −10.0 − (−11.0) = +1.0, loser −12.0 − (−11.5) = −0.5, margin 1.5.
Multiplying by β = 0.1 gives 0.15. This is the same gap a reward model would score, with the implicit reward β × log ratio standing in for r.
The sigmoid of 0.15 is 0.5374, read as the chance the winner is preferred under the implicit reward.
The loss is −ln 0.5374 = 0.6210, down from 0.6931. Small, because β = 0.1 shrinks a margin of 1.5 nats.
The gradient on this pair is scaled by 1 − 0.5374 = 0.4626. Pairs already ranked right get small weight, pairs ranked wrong get weight near 1.
